ASTRA — Reaction-partner memory through organometallic intermediates

1. A stronger chemical construction

The most promising direction is no longer a photocage containing two simultaneously generated radicals. It is a chemically stored reaction partner that can be activated and consumed at different times.

I am selecting the formation of carbon–carbon bonds between primary and tertiary alkyl fragments, particularly the quaternary carbon centres important in pharmaceutical synthesis.

A concrete starting system is an iron–octaethylporphyrin catalyst, Fe(OEP), operating through three chemically distinct states:

FeII(OEP)+e−→FeI(OEP),FeI(OEP)+R1Br→R1−FeIII(OEP)+Br−,R1−FeIII(OEP)+R3∙→R1−R3+FeII(OEP).\begin{aligned} \mathrm{Fe^{II}(OEP)}+e^- &\rightarrow \mathrm{Fe^{I}(OEP)},\\[3pt] \mathrm{Fe^{I}(OEP)}+\mathrm{R^1Br} &\rightarrow \mathrm{R^1{-}Fe^{III}(OEP)}+\mathrm{Br^-},\\[3pt] \mathrm{R^1{-}Fe^{III}(OEP)}+\mathrm{R^3{}^\bullet} &\rightarrow \mathrm{R^1{-}R^3}+\mathrm{Fe^{II}(OEP)}. \end{aligned}FeII(OEP)+e−FeI(OEP)+R1BrR1−FeIII(OEP)+R3∙​→FeI(OEP),→R1−FeIII(OEP)+Br−,→R1−R3+FeII(OEP).​

Here R1R^1R1 denotes a primary alkyl fragment and R3R^3R3 a tertiary alkyl fragment. The last step is bimolecular homolytic substitution, SH2S_H2SH​2, not conventional two-radical recombination.

This chemistry has substantial experimental grounding. Liu and colleagues established primary-alkyl–iron intermediates and their coupling with tertiary radicals in 2021. More importantly, Pace and colleagues demonstrated in 2024 that reduced Fe(I)(OEP) can form Fe(III)–alkyl complexes through substitution of primary alkyl electrophiles, with productive cross-coupling occurring under iron/photoredox conditions. Their system achieved preparatively useful yields and verified iron speciation through spectroscopic and stoichiometric studies.

PMC
+1

The proposed invention is therefore not the Fe–alkyl bond or the SH2S_H2SH​2 reaction. Both are established. It is the attempt to use that intermediate as a controllable chemical memory element: write one molecular partner, preserve it while activation conditions or feed composition change, then consume it selectively and regenerate the catalyst.

This replaces the original requirement for two radical lifetimes to overlap with a more favourable, but still unverified, condition: the stored Fe–alkyl state must survive until the second partner becomes available.

2. The specific write–hold–read cycle

A particularly useful precursor choice is a primary alkyl mesylate for the stored fragment and a tertiary alkyl bromide for the later radical.

This selection matters chemically. A primary mesylate can react with reduced Fe(I) through the established substitution pathway, without requiring a free primary radical as an intermediate. The tertiary bromide can instead undergo halogen-atom transfer from a photogenerated silyl radical. Those different activation mechanisms give a possible way to distinguish the two partners.

Pace et al.'s 2024 chemistry already supplies an important compatible-environment starting point: Fe(OEP), iridium photocatalysis, aminosilane, tertiary bromides and primary alkyl mesylates or bromides under blue illumination in acetone. Reported experiments included 450 nm irradiation and 10 mol% iron catalyst. The paper also demonstrated formation of Fe–alkyl from independently prepared Fe(I) and a primary mesylate.

pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov

This supplies more than a hypothetical combination of independently successful reagents. Nevertheless, the published reaction operates with coupling partners together; it does not establish that a separately loaded Fe–alkyl population can survive a deliberate holding interval and then execute repeated, temporally separated cycles.

There is also a reason not to rely merely on withholding the tertiary bromide during an illuminated writing stage. Without it, the photogenerated silyl radicals can follow other reaction pathways and consume reagent. An independently controlled electrochemical Fe(I)-generation step could offer a cleaner writing operation, but compatibility with the complete photochemical readout cycle has not been demonstrated.

The strongest immediate chemical construction is therefore the known homogeneous Fe(OEP) reaction environment, initially tested through isolated or independently generated Fe–alkyl states. Electrochemical writing and spatially separated production zones are extensions, not premises of the first result.

The answer is not established by observing an Fe–alkyl intermediate.

Two older primary studies expose a serious vulnerability. Song and Goff reported room-temperature Fe–C homolysis accompanied by alkyl-group crossover between iron porphyrins. Riordan and Halpern subsequently investigated the Fe–C dissociation kinetics of several alkyliron porphyrins. They reported ligand-dependent dissociation barriers and found that additional axial ligands could accelerate Fe–C homolysis.

There are two different meanings of chemical memory:

Fragment memory: The catalyst population retains the desired AAA fragment until BBB arrives. An AAA radical could dissociate and rebind a different iron centre without destroying this form of memory.

This yields an intriguing physical possibility: a chemically labile Fe–C bond could still support relatively persistent partner memory if most dissociation events are followed by rapid local recapture.

The useful design variable is not simply Fe–C bond strength. It is the probability that a temporarily dissociated fragment returns to the same useful chemical state rather than becoming lost or redistributed.

One construction worth developing is a peripherally anchored iron porphyrin in a permeable, non-coordinating organic environment. Peripheral anchoring would immobilize the catalyst without deliberately installing strongly coordinating axial groups, which the older dissociation results warn may destabilize stored alkyl species.

The environment must still permit primary-mesylate access to Fe(I), tertiary-radical access to Fe(III)–alkyl, and release of the neutral coupling product. A particularly important negative conclusion follows: if the simultaneous 2024 Fe(OEP) reaction already maintains the same population of Fe–alkyl intermediate under an equivalent tertiary-radical flux, temporally separating the operations provides no intrinsic bond-forming selectivity advantage.

It may actually reduce productivity because the loaded catalyst waits without forming product and can lose stored material during that interval.

The scientific justification for the invention must therefore be a genuinely different operation: delayed partner selection, preservation of chemically reactive inventory, independently addressable reaction sites, or productive transformations involving reagents that cannot safely coexist during simultaneous activation.

None has yet been demonstrated here.

8. Where the research now stands

The physical construction has advanced from a generic confinement sketch to a chemically grounded Fe(OEP)-mediated pathway, with an experimentally supported primary-alkyl loading mechanism, tertiary-radical activation pathway,

The new mathematical results expose an additional constraint beyond radical escape: finite chemical storage must be read before it decays, while nearly complete inventory depletion incurs an increasing radical-consumption penalty. Reprogramming between different stored fragments may require a distinct clearing or resetting operation.

The strongest next uncertainty is whether an alkyl–Fe(OEP) intermediate has a sufficiently favourable ratio of productive tertiary-radical substitution to irreversible loss under one common operating environment, including illumination and multiple catalyst cycles.

If that ratio is favourable but site identity is unstable, the next scientifically justified construction is localized geminate protection through a non-coordinating environment. If the ratio is unfavourable even in homogeneous solution, introducing a scaffold prematurely is unlikely to solve the problem; the chemical activation or storage species should change.

No new laboratory kinetics or physical turnover data have been obtained. The supported advance is a specific chemical mechanism, its quantitative operating constraints and a sharper distinction between ordinary radical sorting and programmable chemical memory. Whether that distinction can become an enabling manufacturing capability remains the central research question.
